items.title: Albert Morgan Interview, 1958-08-19
items.q: Yeah, oh, Billy Banks, all the Dixieland group. I made a lot of recordings with them

ctx.x: Because he really, he really did. He helped me. He drilled me from, from the time, from seven o'clock in the morning up until noon, it's time to eat. Then, then the big band rehearsals, see. But, what he used to do, he marked, marked my music, and where, marked the fingering on my instrument. Then I knew a little bass horn, I could play it on either instrument then, see. I got so, coming up, the bass horn, and, and the bass string bass. Because I, I knew, I, I, there's one good thing about it. I started learning…
I remember those records you made with, um, Red Allen.

Yeah, oh, Billy Banks, all the Dixieland group. I made a lot of recordings with them, and I played with some of the best bands in different combinations. Tommy Dossie, Mount, Mount City Blue Blows, Tommy Dossie, all those guys, Coleman Hawkins.
